summary: Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an immersive web-based simulation that transforms authentic NASA datasets—including ISS telemetry, astronaut biometrics, and 3D station blueprints—into three interactive training modules: microgravity fitness, space nutrition, and station maintenance. Designed for students and aspiring explorers, it places players aboard a realistic virtual ISS where they manage real-time biometrics, calculate caloric needs in zero-g, and repair life-support systems using actual structural schematics. Adaptive AI models trained on NASA health data drive dynamic physics and physiological responses, so every decision produces scientifically grounded feedback. By turning open space-agency data into hands-on gameplay, the trainer makes orbital mechanics, biology, and engineering tangible and engaging for the next generation of space explorers.
details:
The "Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer" is an immersive, gamified simulation designed to prepare the next generation of space explorers. By transforming authentic NASA datasets into interactive modules, the application educates users on the realities of microgravity physics, space nutrition, and station maintenance through engaging, hands-on gameplay.

Detailed Project Description
Our solution bridges the gap between complex space science and accessible education. The application places users in the role of a junior astronaut in training aboard a meticulously modeled virtual space station. Players navigate through distinct mission modules:

Physical Fitness Training: Players manage biometrics, muscle mass, and stamina while operating zero-gravity exercise equipment modeled after real orbital hardware.

Space Nutrition: Users calculate caloric intake and safely handle floating water and food supplies without contaminating the station environment.

Station Maintenance: The simulation requires users to navigate complex, cylindrical modules to repair critical life-support hardware using actual structural blueprints.

Each module translates dense scientific concepts into actionable mechanics, ensuring that players learn practical orbital mechanics, biology, and engineering as they progress to earn their Junior Astronaut certification.

Space Agency Data Used
Our simulation relies heavily on open-source intelligence retrieved directly from the official NASA data portal (https://data.nasa.gov/dataset/).

ISS Telemetry & Trajectory Coordinates: Integrated into the game engine to create accurate orbital mechanics, dynamic lighting, and environmental conditions.

Astronaut Biometric Datasets: Used to train the AI/ML models that govern player stamina, bone density decay, and workout effectiveness in the fitness module.

3D Space Station Blueprints & Imagery: Referenced to build hyper-realistic structural models for the station maintenance and galley environments.

Technology Stack & Team Roles (Team PromptX)
The development of this application required a multi-disciplinary approach across our team to merge raw data with high-fidelity media:

Content Development (Dipayan Pramanik): Leveraged a strong foundation in Electrical and Electronic Engineering and web development to architect the core educational pathways, ensuring technical accuracy perfectly aligns with engaging gameplay loops.

AI/ML Data Training (Shimul Raj Das): Processed raw NASA telemetry and biometrics to create adaptive in-game physics and responsive AI behaviors.

Full Stack Development (Hemel Shikder): Bridged the game engine with live API databases to ensure seamless real-time data integration and platform stability.

Media Engineering (Afsana Tahsin Khan): Implemented spatial audio and realistic soundscapes to enhance environmental immersion in a microgravity setting.

Video Engineering (Anamika Biswas): Rendered high-fidelity 3D cinematic visuals and intuitive user interfaces.

Project Journey & Challenges Overcome
Our collaborative methodology was driven by structured technical leadership and community engagement practices, allowing us to coordinate a complex, multi-disciplinary pipeline efficiently. The core inspiration for the Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer was the realization that while NASA provides incredible open data, raw datasets can be intimidating for students to interpret.

Our primary technical challenge was translating massive spreadsheets of ISS telemetry and astronaut health metrics into intuitive, responsive game mechanics. We iteratively designed our AI models to parse this data in real-time so the game environment reacts dynamically to the player's choices. Through continuous testing, we refined our 3D environments to precisely match NASA's photographic references of the ISS interior, successfully engineering an experience that is technologically robust, visually stunning, and highly educational.
